comment: Rules for tools/bash_guard.py. Canonical source: Git Crafter. Each rule seeds at least one command it must block and one it must allow; bash_guard.py --self-test runs them all, plus the corpus in bash_guard_cases.json. Every rule names a fix, which tells the agent how to retry (the self-test checks it); a step only the owner can do routes to the orchestrator. bash_guard_rules.local.json beside bash_guard.py, in this format, adds one owner's rules and key_vars at load (BASH_GUARD_LOCAL overrides its path); it never reuses a template id, and the corpus runs against the template alone. Keys: match.program (string or list) and match.sub (subcommand tokens) pick the command. when_any, when_all and unless_any hold conditions: flag, missing_flag, arg_regex (with not_after, operands that follow one of those options do not count), arg_in, path_in, has_positional, joined_regex, env_regex, push_from_branch, lead_flag, no_args, flag_value_not, flag_last_value_not (the same test on the last copy, as gh reads it), flag_last_off (a boolean flag ends off: its last copy reads off, --x --x=false, or no copy is left once option values are skipped, -A --x; value_opts and value_short name the options whose values are skipped), always. A condition may add sub, sub_in or program_in to narrow it. For git, a flag in when_any or when_all also matches an abbreviation of a long option (git takes any unambiguous prefix: --no-verif, --har, --forc); unless_any and missing_flag need the exact spelling. A flag given as --flag=false, 0, no or off is off and the scan goes on; any_value marks a flag whose value is not a boolean (--force-with-lease=<ref>). kind=heredoc checks unquoted heredoc bodies with body_regex. kind=pipe checks a pipeline, a $(...) handed to a shell, or a process substitution, for an upstream program feeding a downstream one. lead_flag checks an option before the subcommand (security -i); no_args holds when the command has no arguments. A shell or python running a script file the rules name is matched as that script too (bash keys.sh run, python3 tools/claude_os_sync.py apply). kind=path checks every operand, the text after = or a leading @ in one, input redirections, wrapper and assignment tokens, and path literals in one-liners run by code_readers. A program on its metadata list only looks at names, so its operands do not count. paths use this notation: ~/x under the home folder, //**/x anywhere on disk, ** for any folders. source names the canonical list. log_command false keeps a rule's command text out of bash_guard.log, for rules whose command can carry a key value. match.any_program true matches every command, a bare assignment included. word_in holds when any argument, option values included, is one of its words. key_var tests the key variables in the top-level key_vars: names lists common secret variables, and patterns name a key by its suffix. An owner adds its own in the local rules file, or sets BASH_GUARD_KEYS to a keys.toml registry, whose [[var]] names and aliases the guard adds on each run (a format = "public" row holds an id, not a key, and is left out). Its modes: expanded, an argument expands one ($NAME, ${NAME...}, zsh's ${(U)NAME}, but not ${#NAME}, ${+NAME} or ${NAME:+word}, which print no value); named, an operand is one; assigned, an argument gives one a value or expands one; env, an assignment before the program, or alone, does. An empty value (NAME=) sets none. past_help true also keeps a rule on when the command holds --help, which otherwise skips every simple rule: echo prints the word with the value, a credential helper reads argv[1] and ignores the rest, macOS rm stops reading options at the first operand, and git, gh and find can take --help as an option value (git commit -m --help). A past_help rule still skips a plain help call: only --help and words the rule names as subcommands (sudo --help, security import --help). A rule leaves past_help off where a help call alone would still match it (gh repo delete --help). resolve_vars_regex reads $NAME or ${NAME} as its value for that rule alone, when the command opens with NAME=value (ended by ;, && or a newline), the value matches the regex, and nothing later may change it (bash_guard_literals.py).

rules.why: House rule: never force-push.
rules.fix: Push to a new branch name, or add a new commit on top and push normally.

rules.why: House rule: never push to main.
rules.fix: Push your branch by name (git push -u origin <branch>) and open a pull request.

rules.why: Hooks are gates, and skipping one hides a failure.
rules.fix: Run it again without the skip, then fix what the hook reports.

rules.why: Exporting a hook-skip variable turns gates off for every later commit.
rules.fix: Unset it (unset HUSKY) and let the hooks run.

rules.why: Pointing core.hooksPath anywhere but .githooks turns the repo's gates off.
rules.fix: Leave core.hooksPath at .githooks.

rules.why: Removing or renaming the core section drops core.hooksPath and turns the repo's gates off; renaming another section to core can set it.
rules.fix: Leave the core section in place, and unset only the key you mean (git config --unset core.<key>).

rules.why: House rule: never hard-reset.
rules.fix: Commit work in progress, then use git revert or start a fresh branch from origin/main.

rules.why: Checking out or restoring the whole tree throws away every uncommitted change for good.
rules.fix: Commit the work in progress (git commit -m wip) or name the files you mean to discard.

rules.why: xargs hands git restore, or git checkout --, paths the guard cannot see, so it may restore the whole work tree, the outcome git-discard-all stops.
rules.fix: Restore the files by name (git restore src/a.ts), or unstage only (xargs git restore --staged). To drop all changes, ask first; the work is not recoverable.

rules.why: A word in git restore that the guard cannot read ($(...), backticks or a variable) may be -W, so restoring '.' with --staged may still restore the work tree, the outcome git-discard-all stops.
rules.fix: Write the flags out: git restore --staged . unstages only.

rules.why: Restoring the whole tree throws away every uncommitted change for good. -W inside a cluster (-qW, -WS) restores the work tree beside --staged, and -s or --source takes the next word, so git restore -s -S . restores the work tree.
rules.fix: Commit the work in progress (git commit -m wip) or name the files you mean to discard.

rules.why: git clean -f deletes untracked files for good, and untracked work has no history to recover from.
rules.fix: Run git clean -n to list the files, then delete the exact paths you mean.

rules.why: git clean -f deletes untracked files for good. -e and --exclude take the next word as their pattern, so a -n or --dry-run after them (-fen, -f -e -n, -f --exclude --dry-run) is no dry run, and a -f after -e -- still forces.
rules.fix: Run git clean -n to list the files, then delete the exact paths you mean.

rules.why: git clean -f deletes untracked files for good. -e and --exclude take the next word, -- included, or the rest of their cluster, so git clean -e -- -f and git clean -fe-n are forced cleans that main reads as neither forced nor dry runs.
rules.fix: Run git clean -n to list the files, then delete the exact paths you mean.

rules.why: House rule: never check out one side of a conflict wholesale.
rules.fix: Resolve each conflicted file on its own.

rules.why: House rule: never take one side of a conflict wholesale.
rules.fix: Merge normally and resolve each conflicted file on its own.

rules.why: Merge only the exact commit the reviewer verified. Never turn on auto-merge (house rule), and never bypass protections with --admin.
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this pull request: pass --match-head-commit with the literal head SHA the reviewer verified, and drop --auto and --admin. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.
block: gh pr merge 12 --merge --match-head-commit "$(gh pr view 12 --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)"
S=3f2a9c1d; S=$(git rev-parse HEAD); gh pr merge 12 --squash --match-head-commit $S

rules.why: gh refuses --disable-auto beside --auto or --admin, so the --disable-auto exemption never covers either.
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this pull request: pass --match-head-commit with the literal head SHA the reviewer verified, and drop --auto and --admin. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.

rules.why: gh reads only the last copy of --disable-auto, so --disable-auto=false after it merges, and the --disable-auto exemption does not cover that merge.
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this pull request: pass --match-head-commit with the literal head SHA the reviewer verified, and drop --auto and --admin. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.

rules.why: gh keeps the last --match-head-commit, so a second copy after the reviewed SHA (--match-head-commit <sha> --match-head-commit "$SHA") pins whatever the checkout's head is.
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this pull request: pass --match-head-commit with the literal head SHA the reviewer verified, and drop --auto and --admin. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.

rules.why: Merging through the API skips the head-commit check, and enabling auto-merge breaks a house rule.
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this pull request: use gh pr merge N --<method> --match-head-commit with the literal head SHA the reviewer verified (or SHA=<it>; at the start of the command, then $SHA), and drop --auto and --admin. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.
block: gh api graphql -f query='mutation { mergePullRequest(input: {pullRequestId: "x"}) { clientMutationId } }'
SHA=main; gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge -f sha=$SHA
false && SHA=3f2a9c1d; gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge -f sha=$SHA
SHA=3f2a9c1d; gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge -f sha=$SHA -f sha=zz
allow: gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge -f sha=3f2a9c1d -f merge_method=squash

rules.why: gh stack merge takes no head SHA (GitHub Docs, stacked PRs CLI commands, read 2026-11-11), so it merges whatever each layer's head is when it runs, not the commit the reviewer verified.
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this stack: merge it with gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/N/merge-async -f sha=<the literal head SHA the reviewer verified> -f merge_method=<method>, N being the top layer to merge, and no bypass_rules. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.

rules.why: The asynchronous merge API, the one way a stack merges, takes bypass_rules, which skips the repository rules a merge must meet (GitHub Docs, REST pulls, read 2026-11-11).
rules.fix: Only if rules/delegation.md lets this session merge this stack: merge it with gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/N/merge-async -f sha=<the literal head SHA the reviewer verified> -f merge_method=<method>, N being the top layer to merge, and no bypass_rules. Otherwise stop at the open pull request for the orchestrator.
block: gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge-async -f sha=3f2a9c1d -F bypass_rules=true
gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge-async -f sha=3f2a9c1d -F bypass_rules=false -F bypass_rules=true
gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge-async -f sha=3f2a9c1d --field bypass_rules=1
allow: gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/12/merge-async -f sha=3f2a9c1d -F bypass_rules=false

rules.why: A gh api write to secrets, to main's ref or to the merges endpoint reaches a door another rule guards: secrets are the owner's, main takes no push, and a merge needs the reviewed head. Org and repo rulesets and branch protection are the session's to change (the owner, 2026-11-09, #430); a delete is the owner's; its Settings page measures drift.
rules.fix: Read with a plain gh api GET. A secret change is the owner's. Change a repo's rulesets or branch protection with gh api -X PUT, POST or PATCH on repos/<owner>/<repo>/rulesets or branches/<branch>/protection. A merge goes through gh pr merge with --match-head-commit, and only where rules/delegation.md lets this session merge.
block: gh api -X PATCH repos/o/r/git/refs/heads/main -f sha=x -F force=true
gh api -X POST repos/o/r/merges -f base=main -f head=x
gh api -X POST https://api.github.com/repos/o/r/merges -f base=main -f head=x
gh api -X POST repos/$R/merges -f base=main -f head=x

rules.why: Deleting an org or repo ruleset, or a repo's branch protection, drops every merge rule it held at once, so one runs only with its reason on the command; a PUT that changes one can be read and reverted.
rules.fix: Change the ruleset or protection with gh api -X PUT or PATCH instead, for example enforcement set to disabled for a ruleset. A one-way delete is the session's once it has read the target and checked nothing uses it: put the reason on the command, ONE_WAY_REASON="why this goes" before the program, and for gh api the path before -X DELETE (the owner, 2026-11-10; rules/delegation.md).
allow: ONE_WAY_REASON="duplicate of ruleset 2, same rules" gh api repos/o/r/rulesets/1 -X DELETE

rules.why: These GraphQL mutations reach the doors gh-api-write-door guards: they move or delete a ref, merge one branch into another, commit to a branch without a push, or delete a branch protection rule or ruleset. Creating or updating one is the session's (the owner, 2026-11-05).
rules.fix: Push a branch with git and open a pull request. Change a protection rule or ruleset with its update mutation; deleting one is the owner's; a merge goes through gh pr merge with --match-head-commit, and only where rules/delegation.md lets this session merge.

rules.why: Deleting a repo, and DELETE calls to the GitHub API, cannot be undone from here, so one runs only with its reason on the command. Creating, publishing and archiving are allowed.
block: export ONE_WAY_REASON=later; gh repo delete owner/x --yes
allow: ONE_WAY_REASON="empty test repo, no clones, no deploys" gh repo delete owner/x --yes
ONE_WAY_REASON="stale comment, replaced by 123" gh api repos/o/r/issues/comments/1 -X DELETE
rules.fix: To retire a repo, archive it (gh repo archive). To correct a comment, post a new one. To delete a branch whose pull request is closed and holds its tip, so GitHub can restore it, run git push origin --delete <branch>. A one-way delete is the session's once it has read the target and checked nothing uses it: put the reason on the command, ONE_WAY_REASON="why this goes" before the program, and for gh api the path before -X DELETE (the owner, 2026-11-10; rules/delegation.md).

rules.why: Printing a GitHub token puts it in the transcript.
rules.fix: gh is already signed in; call gh api or gh pr directly without reading the token.
block: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) gh api user

rules.why: git credential fill and a credential helper's get print the stored GitHub credential, a token included, in the tool output. A helper reads argv[1] and ignores the rest, so --help after get still prints it (git-credential-osxkeychain.c upstream). A session never holds a key value (rules/keys.md).
rules.fix: git and gh are already signed in: run git push, git fetch or gh directly without reading the credential.

rules.why: A sign-in is a step the platform keeps human, and a secret's value on the command line lands in the transcript (rules/delegation.md). A session sets a secret by piping the value from where it is issued, never printed (the owner, 2026-11-11). Removing a secret holds no value, so a session removes a repo's secret that no workflow reads (the owner, 2026-11-10); the Settings tab counts them.
block: gh secret set API_KEY --body abc123 -R o/r
openssl rand -hex 32 | gh secret set K --org o
gh api -X POST /app-manifests/abc123/conversions --jq .pem | gh secret set K -u
allow: gh secret remove OLD_TOKEN --env production -R o/r
gh api -X POST /app-manifests/abc123/conversions --jq .pem | gh secret set BOARD_APP_KEY -R o/r
rules.fix: gh is already signed in: use it as is. To set a secret, pipe the value from its issuer into gh secret set NAME -R owner/repo, never --body and never printed. Removing a repo's secret that no workflow reads is the session's: gh secret delete NAME -R owner/repo. An organization's or a user's secret binds more than one repo and stays the owner's.

rules.why: A GitHub App manifest conversion returns the app's private key, client secret and webhook secret. Printed, saved or teed, the key lands in the transcript or on disk (rules/keys.md: a session never holds a key value). A store reads only that pipe or a fresh openssl rand value; any other source (a file, a heredoc, echo, curl) is a value that sat on disk, on the command line or with someone else.
rules.fix: Pipe it straight into its store, as the pipeline's last stage: gh api -X POST /app-manifests/CODE/conversions --jq .pem | gh secret set NAME -R owner/repo. Read the client ID afterwards with gh api apps/SLUG --jq .client_id.
block: gh api -X POST /app-manifests/abc123/conversions --jq .pem | tee k | gh secret set K -R o/r
gh api -X POST /app-manifests/abc123/conversions --jq .pem >&2 | gh secret set K -R o/r
gh secret set K -R o/r < k.txt
gh secret set K -R o/r <<< abc123
printf abc123 | gh secret set K -R o/r

gh secret set K -R o/r <<EOF
abc123
EOF
cat k.txt | gh secret set K -R o/r
curl -s https://example.com/k | gh -R o/r secret set K
bash -c 'echo abc123 | gh secret set K -R o/r'
openssl rand -out k 32 | gh secret set K -R o/r
openssl rand --writerand k 32 | gh secret set K -R o/r
openssl rand -hex 32 > k | gh secret set K -R o/r
allow: gh api -X POST /app-manifests/abc123/conversions --jq .pem | gh secret set BOARD_APP_KEY -R o/r
gh api -X POST app-manifests/abc123/conversions --jq .pem 2>/dev/null | gh secret set K -R o/r
openssl rand -hex 32 | gh secret set WEBHOOK_SECRET -R o/r

rules.why: sudo here has no terminal to ask for the password in, and the admin password is the owner's to type (rules/delegation.md).
allow: echo 'run sudo softwareupdate as the admin'
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && echo yes || echo no
rules.fix: Do it with your own account's rights: a path in your home or the repo, a tool's own updater, or a cloud lane. Claude holds no standing admin rights (the owner, 2026-11-07). Root work is the owner's one-time approval (rules/delegation.md, Owner's queue): say in chat what it changes, and only after his yes run osascript -e 'do shell script "CMD" with prompt "Claude wants to: WHAT IT CHANGES" with administrator privileges' once. Never a command for him to type. Inside it, sudo -u USER -H CMD runs a step as that user.

rules.why: macOS's admin dialog shows only its prompt, not the command, so the prompt must say what changes. The admin password is the owner's to type in that dialog, never on a command line.
block: osascript -e 'do shell script "chown me /x" with administrator privileges'
osascript -e 'do shell script "chown me /x" with prompt "Claude wants to: own /x" with administrator privileges password "hunter2"'
osascript -e 'do shell script "chown me /x" with prompt "Claude wants to: own /x" user name "admin" password "hunter2" with administrator privileges'
osascript -e 'do shell script "chown me /x" with administrator privileges' --help
allow: osascript -e 'do shell script "chown me /x" with prompt "Claude wants to: own /x" with administrator privileges'
osascript -e 'do shell script "sudo -u someone -H /opt/homebrew/bin/brew upgrade --cask sf-symbols" with prompt "Claude wants to: update SF Symbols" with administrator privileges'
rules.fix: Only after the owner's yes in chat to this one change (rules/delegation.md, Owner's queue), run osascript -e 'do shell script "CMD" with prompt "Claude wants to: WHAT IT CHANGES" with administrator privileges' once, as one AppleScript statement, with no password or user name clause.

rules.why: Deleting a Worker, a database, a bucket, a namespace, a queue or a secret cannot be undone, so one runs only with its reason on the command. Deploys, setting secrets and remote writes that delete nothing are allowed.
block: npx wrangler kv key delete --binding KV k --remote
wrangler pages secret delete API_KEY --project-name site
wrangler secrets-store secret delete store1 --secret-id s1
REASON="not the marker" wrangler d1 delete site-db
allow: npx wrangler kv key put --binding KV k v --local
npx wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --env staging --remote
ONE_WAY_REASON="preview database, replaced by site-db" wrangler d1 delete site-db-preview
rules.fix: Deploys, secrets and writes that delete nothing stay allowed. A one-way delete is the session's once it has read the target and checked nothing uses it: put the reason on the command, ONE_WAY_REASON="why this goes" before the program (the owner, 2026-11-10; rules/delegation.md).

rules.why: find with -delete, or -exec rm, from the home folder or the root deletes the tree under it, the outcome rm-root stops.
rules.fix: Name the narrower folder the files are in (find ./build -name '*.pyc' -delete), or list them first with -print and delete that list.

rules.why: Recursive delete of a root, home, current or parent directory.
rules.fix: Name the exact path, such as rm -rf /tmp/scratch/*.

rules.why: Running a script straight from the network skips review, and machine policy forbids vendor installers.
rules.fix: Download the script to a file and read it before you run it, or install the tool from its package manager.

rules.why: An unquoted heredoc runs backticks in its body as commands, and this once ran a sudo rm -rf. A backslash-escaped backtick is a plain character, so it passes (8 of 8 blocks from 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-03 were escaped ones).
rules.fix: Quote the delimiter (<<'EOF'), escape each backtick as \`, or write the file with the Write tool.
block:
cat > notes.md <<EOF
Use `git status` first.
EOF

cat > notes.md <<EOF
One \`safe\` and one `id`
EOF
allow:
cat > notes.md <<'EOF'
Use `git status` first.
EOF

gh pr create --title t --body "$(cat <<EOF
| \`chart: flow\` | ${n} open |
EOF
)"

rules.why: Machine policy: no new LaunchAgents or LaunchDaemons.
rules.fix: Schedule it as a GitHub Actions workflow, or send the orchestrator the job and why for a Claude scheduled task.

rules.why: Machine policy: no scheduled jobs on this Mac outside Claude scheduled tasks.
rules.fix: Schedule it as a GitHub Actions workflow, or send the orchestrator the job and why for a Claude scheduled task.

rules.why: security find-*-password with -w or -g prints the key value, and dump-keychain -d prints every value.
rules.fix: Drop -w and -g: security find-generic-password -s NAME shows that the item exists without its value. Or run bash keys.sh check.
block: KEY=$(security find-generic-password -s X -w) runpodctl get pod
allow: security find-generic-password -s API-Key-RunPod -a RUNPOD_API_KEY >/dev/null && echo present
echo 'the owner runs: security find-generic-password -s X -w'

rules.why: Adding or deleting a Keychain item creates or removes a key, a step the owner does (rules/delegation.md). A session once overwrote a real item this way.
block: security export -k login.keychain -t identities -f pkcs12 -o out.p12
allow: echo 'the owner runs security -i in Terminal.app'
rules.fix: Check a key with the account's keys check line (~/.claude/code-os/account.json). To add or remove one, send the orchestrator its name as account.json's naming says.

rules.why: The clipboard can hold a key the owner just copied.
block: osascript -e 'set x to the clipboard' -e 'return x'
allow: osascript -e 'display notification "Copied to the clipboard" with title "x"'
rules.fix: Read the file or the command output you need directly, never the clipboard.

rules.why: Printing the environment prints every exported value with it, keys included.
rules.fix: Check one variable without printing it: [ -n "$NAME" ] && echo set.
allow: echo 'never run printenv or bare env'
git commit -m 'block env and printenv dumps'

rules.why: Expanding a key variable in echo, printf or print puts its value in the tool output, and declare -p, typeset NAME and zsh's typeset -m print it too. A session never holds a key value (rules/keys.md).
rules.fix: Check it without printing the value: [ -n "$NAME" ] && echo set, or ${#NAME} for its length.

rules.why: A key variable given a value puts the key on the command line, in the transcript and the process list, and one copied into another variable is a step from printing it. A session never holds a key value (rules/keys.md).
rules.fix: Run the command through the account's keys use line (~/.claude/code-os/account.json, such as keys exec <software>:<purpose> -- <command>), which passes the key without showing it.

rules.why: That path can hold a key value, and a session never reads one.
rules.fix: To check that the file exists, use ls, test -e or stat. A command that needs a key from it runs through the account's keys use line (~/.claude/code-os/account.json). For other facts in ~/.claude.json, such as Claude Code's flag cache, run python3 -I ~/.claude/code-os/json_facts.py claude FIELD, which never prints a string value.
rules.source: Common credential locations of widely used CLIs and dotfiles. An owner adds its own paths as a path rule in the local rules file.

rules.why: A key on the command line lands in the transcript, the shell history and the process list.
block: modal secret create --force -e main kit KIT_API_KEY=abc
allow: git commit -m 'never pass --apiKey to runpodctl config'
rules.fix: Pass the key through the account's keys use line (~/.claude/code-os/account.json), so it never appears on the command line.

rules.why: These commands print a stored token, or rewrite the file that holds one. gh auth token is gh-token-print.
rules.fix: The CLI is already signed in: run the command you need without printing its token. For a token change, send the orchestrator what and why.
allow: git commit -m 'block wrangler auth token and modal config show'

rules.why: claude setup-token mints a long-lived Claude Code OAuth token and prints it in the tool output. A session never holds a key value (rules/keys.md).
allow: echo 'the owner runs claude setup-token in Terminal.app'
rules.fix: Use the Claude Code sign-in this session already has. If a long-lived token is truly needed, send the orchestrator why; minting one is a sign-in step the owner does (rules/delegation.md).

rules.why: claude_os_sync.py apply installs the files the reviewed manifest.json lists into ~/.claude, and only from a clean main equal to origin/main; the orchestrator runs it after each merge that changes tier 1 (rules/delegation.md). --manifest swaps in a file list nobody reviewed, and --repo-path into ~/.claude points another repo's files at the config every session reads. The script refuses both too; the guard also covers copies that lack that check.
rules.fix: Run apply without them: python3 -I <Git Crafter checkout>/tools/claude_os_sync.py apply user-claude --yes. A new file list goes into manifest.json by pull request.
block: uv run tools/claude_os_sync.py apply user-claude --yes --manifest m.json

rules.why: Cloud first: a full test suite runs in the cloud, never on this machine. A run that names one test file stays local, and so does node --test on one sub-folder at least two deep (the owner, 2026-11-11) or one given a single shell variable, since the guard cannot tell what it holds (rules/compute.md).
rules.fix: Run the suite in the cloud: push the branch, then read gh pr checks and gh run view --log, or start gh workflow run cloud-test.yml where the repo has it. On this Mac, name one test file instead (node --test path/a.test.mjs, npx vitest run path/a.test.ts), or one test sub-folder: node --test quality/render/.

allow: gh workflow run cloud-test.yml -f ref=feat/x -f script=test:unit
echo 'never run npm test or pytest on this Mac'
git commit -m 'run npm test in CI, not on the Mac'
for f in pages/actions/page.test.ts core/charts/render.test.ts; do timeout 30 node --test $f; done

rules.why: Cloud first: builds, browsers and e2e, renders, GPU work and local model inference run in the cloud, not on this machine (rules/compute.md).
rules.fix: Run it in the cloud. Builds and e2e: push the branch, then read gh pr checks and gh run view --log. Comfy: comfy run --where cloud, under the tiers in rules/comfy.md. Other renders, GPU work and models: the cloud lanes rules/compute.md names, after the owner's yes for anything that spends. Never a card-billed meter.
allow: echo 'never run npm run build, ffmpeg or mlx_lm here'

key_vars.source: Common secret variable names of widely used tools. An owner adds its own in the local rules file, or through BASH_GUARD_KEYS.
